summary: Tabs and the split. New workbench/split_qt.py. Views opened through the navigation (board, tree, Search, Back/Forward) are named working tabs: never the Preview, so the specification and the worksheet stay open together. No duplicate tab: an object open in either pane is brought to the front (navigation pre-check, plus a safety net in WorkspaceTabs.addTab). A two-pane split: Split / One pane on the centre bar; Split / Show beside / Move to the other pane / Bring into focus / Close on a tab's right-click; Open beside on a tile's right-click; a tab dragged out of its strip onto the empty half; a tile dragged off the board onto its half. At most two panes; the divider moves; One pane keeps every tab. host.tabs is always the pane in focus: a click (or a user focus) in the other pane exchanges the two panes' tabs and their slots, so nothing moves on screen while the tree highlight (L1 sync, depth split, pane left/right/top/bottom), her "this" (current_item, the This: words via the centre bar, a staC "this" via field_page.expand_this, split_qt.this_object), Save, the centre bar, Board and Close all follow the pane in focus. The passive pane keeps its page and scroll and carries a quiet mark (◇ Beside · another object; ◆ In focus on the other). Under 2 x 560 px (1366 wide) the panes stack and Side by side is offered. Closing a view inside the split gives its place to the views still open there (never the board or Home). Smoke: 33/33 in graphite and in kasandra, both sizes. Built, not tested in the owner's sense; nothing ran on the ThinkPad.

decisions: host.tabs is always the pane in focus; activating the other pane exchanges both panes' tabs and their places in the divider (slot sizes kept), so the ~78 places that read host.tabs.currentWidget() (the tree via L1, her "this", centre bar, Save, Board, Close, L4's line) follow the pane in focus without being edited. Places and scroll are remembered and put back around the exchange; L1's snapshot is taken first.

Activation is by the owner's input only: a left-button release, or a FocusIn with a mouse/Tab/Backtab/Shortcut reason, inside the other pane (an app event filter installed only while split); requests made before the last exchange are stale (generation counter). Scrolling the passive pane does not activate it.

"Working tabs": a view opened through the navigation (it gets L1's _living_oid) is marked ledgerWorking: never the Preview, title without "Preview ·", restored as working. Without this the worksheet replaced the specification (the Preview) and no split could hold both.

Split with the view in front: the view used before it goes to the first half (left/top), the one in front to the second, in focus (the paper's day: "keeping the specification visible beside the sheet"). Split on a tab that is not in front: it goes beside the one in front. Nothing else open: an empty half that offers the open views.
Narrow: the panes stack when the centre is under 2 x 560 px + handle; the other pane's corner offers Side by side (or Stack). One pane is on the centre bar only.

Dragging a tile on the board now carries the tile (a drop half over the board's right half: "Drop here: open X beside Y"); the board still pans by dragging empty space and with the wheel. The board in a pane of its own was not built (the board stays the centre's home at board depth).

Closing a view inside the split: the pane shows its next view; its last view gone, one pane with the other's views (depths_qt.closing gives no board target while the split holds views; WorkspaceTabs.tabRemoved collapses at once so close_tab never falls back to Home).
The window's close collapses the split first, so every view is asked about and kept with the session by the existing code (if the close is cancelled the split stays collapsed).
The tab strips have their own right-click menu (CustomContextMenu: the global router stops there); before, a right-click on the strip gave the workspace's empty-place menu.
The old Split Editor (one text shown twice) is kept as the explicit "another view" of a text; it and the new split are never on together.
No Kernel operations were added (window behaviour only), so no registry regeneration.

release_note: Tabs and the split: what you open from the board, the tree or Search stays open as a named working tab, and an open object is never opened twice. Split (on the bar above the work, a tab's right-click, a tile's Open beside, or a tab or tile dragged onto the empty half) shows two views side by side, stacked on a narrow screen; the pane you click in is the one in focus and drives the tree's highlight and Kasandra's "this", while the other keeps its place and says "Beside · another object". One pane brings them together and keeps every tab. Built, not tested.
